akhfash:7-7.t: And He said ﴿بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ﴾ when he makes "القَبَسَ" (the firebrand) a badal (substitute) for "الشِّهابِ" (the flame); if he annexes "الشِّهابَ" to "القَبَسِ", he does not put tanwīn on "الشِّهابَ". Both are good.

akhfash:8-8.t: He said ﴿نُودِيَ أَن بُورِكَ﴾, i.e. he was called with that.

akhfash:11-11.t: And He said ﴿إَلاَّ مَن ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْناً بَعْدَ سُوۤءٍ﴾ because ﴿إِلاَّ﴾ enters such speech, like the Arabs' saying: "ما أَشْتَكِي إِلاَّ خَيْراً" (I complain of nothing but good). He did not make his saying "إِلاَّ خَيْراً" refer to the complaint; rather, he knew that when he said to them "I complain of nothing" he would be mentioning good of himself. It is as though he said "I mention nothing but good".

akhfash:13-13.t: And He said ﴿آيَاتُنَا مُبْصِرَةً﴾, i.e. they make them see until they saw. If you wish you say ﴿مُبْصَرَةً﴾ with fatḥa; some people have read it so, and it is good, meaning "made visible, made clear".

akhfash:16-16.t:
And He said ﴿عُلِّمْنَا مَنطِقَ ٱلطَّيْرِ﴾ because, since they spoke to them, it became like speech. The poet said [in the khafīf metre; this is poetic witness no. 233]:
* صدّها منطق الدجاج عن القصد *
(The speech of the hens turned her away from her purpose.)
And he said [in the rajaz metre; this is poetic witness no. 235]:
* فَصَبَّحَتْ والطَيْرُ لَمْ تَكَلَّم *
(She came in the morning while the birds had not yet spoken.)

akhfash:25-25.t:
And He said ﴿أَلاَّ يَسْجُدُواْ﴾: He means ﴿وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾ so "that they would not prostrate" (لـأَنْ لاّ يَسْجُدُوا). Some read ﴿أَلا يَسْجُدوا﴾ and made it a command, as though he said to them "أَلاَ اسْجُدُوا" (indeed, prostrate!), adding between them the "يَا" of alerting; then he dropped the connective alif in "اِسْجُدُوا" and dropped the alif in "يا" because it was vowelless and met the sīn, so it became ﴿أَلاَ يَسْجُدُوا﴾. In poetry [in the ṭawīl metre; this is poetic witness no. 262]:
أَلاَ يَا سْلِمَى يَا دَاَرَمّيٍ على البِلَى * [وَلاَ زَالَ مُنْهَلاً بِجَرْعَائِكِ القِطْرُ]
(O, be safe, O abode of Mayya, despite decay [and may the rain never cease pouring on your sandy ground].)
It is really: "ألا يا اسْلَمِى".

akhfash:28-28.t: He said ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَٱنْظُرْ مَاذَا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾: ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ﴾ is placed later (in meaning), because the meaning is "so deliver it to them, and see what they return, then turn away from them".

akhfash:30-30.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّهُ مِن سُلَيْمَانَ وَإِنَّهُ بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ﴾ depending on ﴿إِنِّيۤ أُلْقِيَ إِلَيَّ كِتَابٌ﴾: ﴿إِنَّهُ مِن سُلَيْمَانَ﴾ and ﴿وَإِنَّهُ بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ﴾; "بِسْمِ اللهِ" comes first in meaning.

akhfash:40-40.t: And He said ﴿لِيَبْلُوَنِيۤ أَأَشْكُرُ أَمْ أَكْفُرُ﴾, i.e. to see whether I am grateful or ungrateful, like your saying: "جِئْتُ لِأَنْظُرَ أَزَيْدٌ أَفْضَلُ أَمْ عَمْرٌو" (I came to see whether Zayd is better or ʿAmr).

akhfash:47-47.t: And [He said] ﴿قَالُواْ ٱطَّيَّرْنَا بِكَ﴾: he assimilated the tāʾ into the ṭāʾ because it is from its place of articulation; when you begin with it you say "اِطَّيَّرْنا".

akhfash:48-48.t: And He said ﴿تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍ﴾: He used a plural, and they have no singular from its own root, like "ذَوْدٍ" (a small herd of camels).

akhfash:60-60.t: And He said ﴿أَمَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ ... ﴿أَمَّن يَبْدَأُ ٱلْخَلْقَ﴾ until the passage ends: ﴿مَنْ﴾ here is not interrogative, depending on His word ﴿خَيْرٌ أَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾; it is only equivalent to "الّذِي" (the one who).

akhfash:65-65.t: And He said [قُلْ لا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاَتِ والأَرْضِ] ﴿ٱلْغَيْبَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ﴾, as He said ﴿إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ مِّنْهُمْ﴾; in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd it is ﴿قَلِيلاً﴾. (The nominative is) a badal (substitute) for the first, because you have negated (the act) of it and assigned it to the other.

akhfash:72-72.t: And He said ﴿رَدِفَ لَكُم﴾, and we think it is "رَدِفَكُمْ" (it has followed close behind you); he brought in the lām and made the verb reach (its object) through it, as He said ﴿لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ﴾ and ﴿لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ﴾. The Arabs say: "رَدِفَهُ أمْرٌ" (a matter followed him), just as they say "تَبِعَه" and "أَتْبَعَهُ" (it followed him).

akhfash:82-82.t: And He said ﴿أَنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ﴾, i.e. "because the people…" (بأنَّ النَّاسَ). Some read ﴿إِنَّ النَّاسَ﴾, as He said ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ مَا نَعْبُدُهُمْ﴾, whose meaning is only "they say: 'we do not worship them'".
